players.product: AI cloud compute capacity (Colossus and Colossus 2)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results release, figures the call does not state: capex by segment was SI $16,444 million, Space $1,606 million and Connectivity $1,543 million, total $19,593 million (nine months $48,069 million versus $13,846 million); SI revenues were $7.6 billion, up 195% sequentially and 830% year over year, of which advertising revenues $538 million and SI solutions and infrastructure revenues $7,022 million; nameplate compute 1.7 GW versus 1.4 GW at June 30 and 0.6 GW a year earlier, as SpaceX continued the buildout of COLOSSUS II and signed additional cloud services agreements. Balance sheet at September 30, 2026: cash and cash equivalents $51,294 million and marketable securities $38,561 million; deferred revenue $10,784 million current and $6,736 million non-current; nine-month net cash provided by operating activities $13,097 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 capex $19,593 million (SI $16,444 million); SI revenues $7.6 billion (+830% YoY)

players.product: Starlink V3 broadband satellites with laser inter-satellite links (~800 Tbps downlink from 9,600 broadband satellites) and Starlink Mobile direct-to-cell

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results release, Connectivity detail: consumer revenues $3,121 million (up 26% sequentially and 57% year over year) and enterprise and government revenues $2,127 million (up 18% and 91%); Connectivity income from operations $2,367 million (up 99%) and adjusted EBITDA $3,499 million (up 82%). Beyond 13.6 million consumer subscribers SpaceX has hundreds of thousands of enterprise subscribers; over 3,800 aircraft were equipped with Starlink as of September 30, 2026; 11.1K total satellites in orbit (a new definition including de-orbit approved satellites, about 400 more than operational-only) and Starlink coverage in 174 countries (page 2 figure). On October 8, 2026 SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum license portfolio of up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band for its Starlink Mobile strategy, expected to close in the first half of 2027 subject to regulatory and other closing conditions.
quarterly_data.figure: consumer revenues $3,121 million; enterprise and government $2,127 million (+91%); over 3,800 aircraft; up to 14 MHz of 800 MHz spectrum

players.product: Falcon 9 and Starship launch (~2,500 tons a year to orbit via Falcon; launches competing constellations)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results release, Space detail: 12 customer and 23 internal launches carried 476 metric tons to orbit (119 customer, 358 internal); nine months 113 launches and 1,517 metric tons. Launch services revenues $1,130 million and launch and development revenues $637 million; Space R&D $1,225 million as Starship R&D accelerated. Starship Flight 14, the first orbital Starship flight, delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites, representing approximately 10x the downlink capacity added by a Falcon 9 Starlink launch. The release states that the planned Starbase, Louisiana spaceport, designed to support thousands of Starship flights a year, targets its first launch for 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: 476 metric tons to orbit in Q3; 26 Starlink V3 satellites (~10x Falcon 9 downlink capacity); Louisiana first launch targeted for 2029
